source.title: Analyzing Fine-Grained Alignment and Enhancing Vision Understanding in Multimodal Language Models
source.authors: Jia-Chen Jiang; Jin-Xin Zhou; Bo Peng; Xia Ning; Zhi-Hui Zhu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-modal patch-to-word alignment using IoU and cosine similarity, rather than comparing distance structures across independently trained models or sweeping scale.
record.gate_note: The alignment results concern visual patches and LLM word embeddings, so they bear on V2 at this fine-grained level. The paper does not test convergence of inter-model distance geometry, scaling, or whether alignment tracks both models' capabilities. Entropy-compression results, caption-quality scores, and downstream task benchmarks are not rows because they do not themselves measure the claimed alignment.
record.test_reason: The study cites the Platonic hypothesis only as motivation. Its alignment measures concern a projector trained to map CLIP patch embeddings into the Vicuna word-embedding space: caption loss for LLaVA, plus a patch loss that directly maximizes cosine similarity with label word embeddings. The alignment is induced by training on purpose, not measured arising between independently trained models. It does not vary the quality of the vision or language models either. So no version is tested; the results belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the projector compresses visual information and improves patch-level alignment, but that this alignment stays weak and coarse under caption loss. Patch-aligned training strengthens compression and alignment and improves captioning, referring-expression grounding (~16%), VQA (~4%) and instruction-following (~3%) results.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses patch-to-word localization IoU, matching pursuit, and cosine similarity to analyze alignment within MLLMs, and trains a projector with an added patch-alignment loss. It does not reproduce the original cross-model distance-geometry or scale measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: In LLaVA-1.5, caption-trained projector outputs localize objects weakly via LLM word embeddings (mIoU 0.142–0.152 vs random 0.065). An added patch-alignment loss raises this to mIoU 0.279 and cosine similarity to 0.56.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In stitched MLLMs, caption-only projector training yields weak patch-level alignment between vision tokens and LLM word embeddings; explicit patch supervision strengthens it.

fits_no_version.finding: Trained projectors reduce the Von Neumann entropy of vision embeddings (e.g. MLP 4.84 to 2.04), whereas random projectors barely change it (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLLM projectors compress visual embeddings when mapping them into the LLM input space.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (venue stated in supplied metadata); the paper text identifies the manuscript as under review.
record.problems: The principal quantitative alignment evaluation uses 100 COCO 2017 images, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. Multi-semantic alignment evidence is qualitative. The study's patch-to-word alignment measures are not the inter-model distance-geometry measure in the broad Platonic claim.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Entropy reduction, caption metrics, and downstream benchmark scores were excluded because they do not directly measure cross-modal representation alignment.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no comparison of independently trained models.
Never measures alignment between independently trained vision and language models, nor whether it grows as both improve. All measured alignment passes through a projector trained for it.
The projector is a learned stitching map, but loss from mapping is not assessed as interchangeability.
No variation of the similarity measure or the inputs.
No test of plateau or causes of convergence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 labels are withdrawn. The motivating citation of the Platonic hypothesis is not tested, and the authors even note separately pretrained encoders and LLMs need not share a basis. Rows r1/r4 and r2/r5 report identical numbers under different stated datasets (GranDf vs COCO), which should be checked.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no comparison of representations from independently trained models.
Does not test whether alignment rises as both vision and language models improve or scale; measures patch-to-word alignment within MLLMs under projector variants and training stages.
No comparison of seeds, features, or shared subspaces.
Does not test interchangeability or loss from mapping between models' representations.
Does not test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Does not test how alignment changes across similarity measures, settings, or input distributions.
Does not test inter-model convergence, a convergence plateau, or shared-data/objective explanations for it.

rows.subject: P_Random MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured patch-level localization alignment as IoU against ground-truth masks.
rows.note: Random-projector reference for the pretrained and SFT LLaVA projectors.
rows.check: Random-projector IoU inside a stitched MLLM. This is not alignment between independently trained vision and language models, and model quality is not varied. Its values (0.065/0.142) are identical to Table 3's r4/r5 despite a different stated dataset (GranDf vs 100 COCO images), so it may be the same measurement.

rows.subject: P_LLaVA Stage1
rows.operation_detail: Measured patch-level localization alignment as IoU against ground-truth masks.
rows.note: The paper says the pretrained projector improves alignment but describes the LLaVA projector's mIoU as low.
rows.check: The projector is trained to align vision with the LLM (caption loss), so the alignment is induced, not convergent. It does not bear on V2.

rows.subject: P_LLaVA Stage2
rows.operation_detail: Measured patch-level localization alignment as IoU against ground-truth masks.
rows.note: The paper reports a further increase after SFT, while describing the mIoU as low.
rows.check: Stage 2 SFT also trains the projector and LLM jointly, so the alignment is induced. It does not bear on V2.

rows.subject: P_Random
rows.operation_detail: Measured patch-level alignment and vision-text embedding cosine similarity.
rows.check: Random-projector control for a trained-in alignment. It duplicates r1's value; it is unclear whether this is a separate evaluation.

rows.subject: P_LLaVA
rows.operation_detail: Measured patch-level alignment and vision-text embedding cosine similarity.
rows.note: The paper reports improvement over the random projector.
rows.check: Caption-trained projector. The alignment is induced by training, not cross-model convergence. It duplicates r2's value.

rows.subject: P_Patch Aligned
rows.operation_detail: Measured patch-level alignment and vision-text embedding cosine similarity.
rows.note: The paper reports better patch-level alignment than both the random and LLaVA projectors.
rows.check: This is the study's own method, a projector trained with an explicit patch-alignment loss, compared with baselines. It is a method-performance row, not a convergence measurement.

rows.subject: P_Random
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between vision and text embeddings.
rows.note: The cosine-similarity values appear as a detached sequence in the text; mapped in the listed projector order, consistent with the paper's stated Table 3 comparison.
rows.check: Random-projector cosine control. The values are legible in Table 3 (0.06/0.07/0.56), not merely flattened.

rows.subject: P_LLaVA
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between vision and text embeddings.
rows.note: The cosine-similarity values appear as a detached sequence in the text; mapped in the listed projector order, consistent with the paper's stated Table 3 comparison.
rows.check: Cosine similarity for the caption-trained projector. The alignment is induced and does not bear on V2.

rows.subject: P_Patch Aligned
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between vision and text embeddings.
rows.note: The cosine-similarity values appear as a detached sequence in the text; mapped in the listed projector order, consistent with the paper's stated Table 3 comparison.
rows.check: Cosine similarity is essentially the training objective of the patch loss (Eq. 5). This is the study's own method's performance.

rows.subject: LLaVA
rows.operation_detail: Used matching pursuit to identify LLM vocabulary tokens most similar to visual patch embeddings.
rows.measure: Qualitative token-map interpretability across image patches
rows.value: Only partial areas or objects achieve alignment; many patches remain uninterpretable.
rows.note: The text describes LLaVA's multi-semantic alignment as limited.
rows.check: Qualitative token map for the LLaVA projector. The alignment is trained in, and there are no numbers.

rows.subject: PatchAligned LLaVA
rows.operation_detail: Used matching pursuit to identify LLM vocabulary tokens most similar to visual patch embeddings.
rows.measure: Qualitative token-map interpretability across image patches
rows.baseline: LLaVA: only partial areas or objects achieve alignment
rows.note: The text explicitly describes improved alignment across most patches.
rows.check: Qualitative result of the study's own method. Not a convergence test.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Patch-aligned projector versus random and LLaVA projectors on the reported patch-alignment measures
reader_labels.reason: Patch alignment rises from 0.142 to 0.279 in mIoU and the reported cosine similarity rises from 0.07 to 0.56; the paper also describes better qualitative patch coverage (r5-r6, r8-r11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: LLaVA pretrained and SFT projectors, including qualitative multi-semantic alignment
reader_labels.reason: The authors characterize the original projector's alignment as weak, coarse, and low in mIoU; measured alignment remains incomplete in the qualitative analysis (r2-r3, r5, r8, r10).
